title: Forest Neighbours: A Day in the Life of a Red Fox

scenes.heading: A forest begins to wake
scenes.caption: A quiet woodland is full of hidden life
scenes.takeaway: The forest changes with every hour
scenes.narration: As the first light reaches the woodland, the forest begins to stir. Leaves move in the breeze, birds call from the canopy, and small animals leave the shelter of their resting places. One of the forest's most adaptable hunters is preparing for another day: the red fox.

scenes.heading: Meet the red fox
scenes.caption: Alert ears help the fox notice its surroundings
scenes.takeaway: A fox relies on sharp senses and careful movement
scenes.narration: The red fox is known for its russet coat, pointed ears, narrow muzzle and bushy tail. Its ears can turn toward faint sounds, while its eyes and nose help it investigate the world. The thick tail helps with balance and can curl around the body like a warm blanket when the fox rests.

scenes.heading: Every sound is a clue
scenes.caption: The fox pauses, listens and looks around
scenes.takeaway: Listening can reveal prey hidden beneath leaves
scenes.narration: Moving through the undergrowth, the fox slows down. It pauses, lifts its head and listens. A tiny rustle may come from an insect, a bird, or a small mammal moving beneath fallen leaves. Rather than rushing, the fox uses patience to work out where the sound came from.

scenes.heading: Following a scent
scenes.caption: The fox investigates tracks and smells on the ground
scenes.takeaway: Scent helps foxes explore and find food
scenes.narration: At the forest floor, scents tell another story. The fox lowers its nose and sniffs along the ground. It may be following the trail of a mouse, checking a familiar path, or investigating where another animal has passed. Smell is an important part of how foxes explore and communicate.

scenes.heading: A careful hunter
scenes.caption: A fox moves quietly before making a quick pounce
scenes.takeaway: Stealth and timing matter more than speed alone
scenes.narration: When prey is nearby, the fox becomes still and focused. It listens for movement under grass or snow, then may spring forward in a sudden pounce. Small mammals are common food, but foxes are opportunistic and also eat insects, fruit, birds and other available food. Their varied diet helps them survive in changing habitats.

scenes.heading: Life beyond the hunt
scenes.caption: Foxes also rest, play and raise their young
scenes.takeaway: A fox is part of a much larger woodland community
scenes.narration: A fox's day is not only about finding food. It rests in sheltered places, explores its territory and raises its young in a den. Foxes share the forest with deer, owls, insects, fungi and countless plants. Each species has its own role, and the health of one can affect many others.

scenes.heading: A home worth protecting
scenes.caption: Healthy forests provide food, shelter and safe pathways
scenes.narration: As daylight fades, the fox slips deeper into the trees. Its survival depends on connected habitat, places to shelter and enough food. Protecting forests means protecting the many lives woven through them. In a healthy woodland, even a quiet rustle in the leaves can be the beginning of another remarkable story.
